title: Finding things: globs and find
summary: Let the shell expand patterns, and let find search the tree.

steps.title: Globs: the shell expands, not the command
body: When you type `ls *.log`, **bash** replaces `*.log` with the matching names *before* `ls` runs. `ls` just sees `ls app.log error.log`.
| `*` | any run of characters (not a leading `.`, not `/`) |
| `{a,b}` | *brace expansion*: generates `a` and `b`, whether or not they exist |
notes.txt *.md          # no .md file: the pattern stays as-is

steps.prompt: The directory holds `a1.txt a2.txt b1.txt ab.txt c10.txt`. What does `echo [ab]?.txt` print?
steps.explain: `[ab]` is one character from {a, b}, `?` is exactly one more character. `c10.txt` fails the first, and the shell sorts matches alphabetically.

steps.prompt: You run `rm * .bak` (note the space). What happens?
options: Every file in the directory is deleted, then rm complains `.bak` doesn't exist
steps.explain: The space makes two arguments: `*` (everything) and `.bak`. Run `echo rm * .bak` first to see what the shell will actually pass.

steps.title: find: search the tree
body: Globs only look in one directory. `find` walks a whole tree and tests each entry.
find /var/log -name "*.gz"              # by name (quote the glob so find gets it, not bash)
find /tmp -mtime +7                     # modified more than 7 days ago
find . -name "*.log" -exec gzip {} \;   # run a command per match
`locate` is faster (it reads a prebuilt index) but can be stale. `which dotnet` tells you which program a command name runs.

steps.prompt: Find regular **files** under `/srv` ending in `.log` and older than 30 days, then delete them.
steps.explain: Tests are ANDed left to right. Put `-delete` last: find evaluates in order, and `-delete` first would delete everything.

steps.prompt: Match the need to the tool.
pairs: Quickly locate a file anywhere by name

steps.prompt: Arrange a safe workflow for bulk-deleting old temp files.
steps.explain: Look at what matches, count it, then act. The same expression each time, with the destructive action added last.

steps.title: A glob matcher
prompt: Write `bool Glob(string pattern, string name)` supporting `*` (any run, including empty), `?` (one character), `[abc]` and ranges like `[0-9]` inside brackets. Every other character matches itself.
solution: for (int k = n; k <= name.Length; k++)
if (name[n] >= set[i] && name[n] <= set[i + 2]) hit = true;
hints: Recursion on (pattern index, name index) is the clearest approach.
For `*`, try matching the rest of the pattern at every remaining position of the name, including the end.
template: Dojo.Eq("star must reach the end", false, Glob("*.cs", "Program.cs.bak"));
Dojo.Eq("question mark is exactly one", false, Glob("app.log.?", "app.log.10"));
